{{italic title}}
{{Short description|Tamil language book about Arithmetic}}
'''Kaṇita Tīpikai''' ('''Gaṇita Dīpika''') is a [[Tamil language|Tamil]] book authored by Paṇṭala Rāmasvāmi Nāykkar and published in 1825 dealing with [[arithmetic]].<ref name="Vepery">{{cite book |last1=Pantala Ramasvami Naykkar  |title=Kanita Dipikai|date=1825 |publisher=Vepery Mission Press |location=Madras |url=https://archive.org/details/gc-sh10-0105/page/n7/mode/2up?view=theater |access-date=27 June 2024}}</ref> It is the first Tamil book on mathematics ever to be printed and it is the first Tamil book ever to introduce the symbol for [[zero]] and also to discuss the [[decimal]] [[place value notation]]  or positional notation using Tamil numerals.<ref name=Senthil>{{cite book |last1=Senthil Babu |title=Science and the Tamil Society: Issues for consideration |date=2006 |publisher=French Institute of Pondicherry |pages=321–336 |url=https://www.academia.edu/7604889/Science_and_Tamil_Society_Issues_for_Consideration |access-date=28 June 2024}} (Chapter in "Negotiating with the Past: Classical Tamil in Contemporary Tamil" edited by M. Kannan and Carlos Mena)</ref>
[[Iravatham Mahadevan]], a well known Indian epigraphist, and M. V. Bhaskar noted thus in an article published in [[The Hindu]] in December 2011: "The convention of using symbols for 10, 100, and 1000 in expressing the higher numerals was current in Tamil Nadu until the advent of printing and the adoption of the international form of Indian numerals with place-value system."<ref name="Hindu">{{cite journal |last1=Iravatham Mahadevan and M. V. Bhaskar |title=Ancient numbers in the land of Ramanujan |journal=The Hindu |date=29 December 2011 |url=https://www.thehindu.com/features/friday-review/history-and-culture/ancient-numbers-in-the-land-of-ramanujan/article2755518.ece |access-date=27 June 2024}}</ref> Senthi Babu D, a historian and researcher attached to the French Institute of [[Puducherry (city)|Pondicherry]], observes: 
:"Pantulu Ramasamy Naicker authored the first modern arithmetic textbook in Tamil, called the “Kanita Teepikai”, sponsored by the company state, in the year 1825. Interestingly, in his ‘payiram’ to the textbook, he justifies the use of both ‘Aryan language’ and “a bit of kotuntamil” for the sake of “understanding of all”. Ramasamy, one can see, had taken great pains to introduce the notation for zero in Tamil as “0”, which directly brought him to the issue of explaining the concept of place value in numbers. When he had to introduce the concept that the value of a number increases by factors of ten on the left, but decreases when it proceeds to the right, his plea to the reader is to follow the rule as it is a ‘decision of God’."<ref name=Senthil/>

==Full text==

The full text of the book is available for free download in [[Internet Archive]]: {{cite book |last1=Kanita Dipikai |title=Pantala Ramasvami Naykkar |date=1825 |publisher=Vepery Mission Press |location=Madras |url=https://archive.org/details/gc-sh10-0105/page/n7/mode/2up?view=theater |access-date=27 June 2024}}
